fieldMarks: Small frog, 15-33 mm (females slightly larger); colour ranges from black, brown or reddish brown to bright green or grey.
Contrasting stripe from the top of the snout along the back, and a triangular marking between the eyes joined to that stripe.
Darker longitudinal stripe on the rear of the thigh; markedly pointed snout; more slender than the northern cricket frog with longer legs and less toe webbing.
Males have darker throats and a single subgular sac; females have white throats.
behavior: Call is a steady, rapid 'click-click-click' at about one per second, given in choruses in most weather and at any time of day.
Sit-and-wait insectivore; mosquitoes are a large part of the diet; tadpoles are herbivorous.
Active throughout the year; day or night in warm months, probably mostly diurnal in cold months. Good jumper.
habitat: Grassy margins of swamps, marshes, lakes, ponds, streams, ditches, bogs and nearby temporary pools, including open woodland that is not heavily shaded; eggs and larvae develop in shallow water.
range: NatureServe lists it in the southeastern US: Virginia, North and South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana.

lookalikes.name: Northern cricket frog
lookalikes.howToTell: Northern is larger and stockier with a blunter snout, shorter legs, more webbing and more prominent warts.
